title: Two maps on the circle are pointwise equal as soon as they agree at the base point and on the loop
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 309-318: maps on the circle are determined by the value at the base point together with the action on the loop, in the form that two maps with such comparable data are pointwise equal. The proof (source lines 319-325) is short but it is the actual argument rather than a pointer: it applies the induction principle of the circle to the family of equality types between the two maps, reads off the base case as exactly one of the two given data, and then identifies the loop case with the other datum by reducing a transport in a family of path types through two cited transport results. Choosing the right family and reducing the loop case are the substance, and the statement alone does not display them.
